get_book_details.description: What a book in the library is: what it covers, when and where it was written, where it sits in the library, what it is called in Hebrew and what else it is cited as. It also returns the shape of the book (how many chapters, and how many verses in each), which is what a workflow needs to walk through it a chapter at a time.

get_commentary.description: Read what the commentators say about one passage (Rashi, Ramban, Sforno and the rest), with each commentator's remarks kept together and in order. Widen it beyond commentary to the midrash, the Talmud, the halakhic and chasidic works that quote or discuss the same line. Genesis 1:1 alone has over five hundred, so ask for as many as you want to read.

commentaries.translation: IN THE BEGINNING — Rabbi Isaac said: The Torah, which is the Law book of Israel, should have commenced with the verse “This month shall be unto you the first of the months.”
IN THE BEGINNING G-D CREATED. This verse calls aloud for elucidation, for creation is a deep mystery.

description: Read from Sefaria, the free library of Jewish texts: Tanakh, Mishnah, Talmud, Midrash, Halakhah, Kabbalah, Chasidut and more, in the original and in translation. Pull up any passage verse by verse, search the whole library at once, read what the commentators say about a line, follow the daily learning cycles including Daf Yomi and the weekly Torah portion, gather the sources on a theme, look up a Hebrew word in Klein, Jastrow or BDB, and draw a passage at random. Every text comes back with the edition it is from and that edition's licence, so it can be quoted properly. No account or API key is required.
